analysis.investment_thesis: Aegis Logistics has an admirable nine-year record of uninterrupted profit growth — precisely the kind of earnings durability I demand — and its D/E of 0.28 is acceptable, but the market charges 32.4x earnings and 4.19x book value for this privilege, leaving no margin of safety for the disciplined investor. The Graham Number of approximately INR 292 against a market price of INR 709 reveals investors are paying 2.4× intrinsic value.
key_strengths: Nine consecutive years of growing net profit (INR 126 Cr in 2016 → INR 787 Cr in 2025, 22.6% CAGR) — the longest and most consistent earnings record in this group
100% OCF positivity over the last five years with operating cash flow of INR 558 Cr in 2025 — real cash earnings, not accounting artefacts
D/E of 0.28 is below my 0.5 threshold; infrastructure-like LPG terminal business with essential-services characteristics
key_risks: Finance costs have grown 27.9% CAGR to INR 165 Cr in 2025 — rising debt service obligations eating into earnings growth
Total debt jumped from INR 835 Cr (2022) to INR 4,606 Cr (2025, including lease obligations) — balance sheet leverage is accelerating
Revenue is volatile: INR 8,627 Cr (2023) → INR 7,046 Cr (2024) → INR 6,764 Cr (2025) — top-line dependent on commodity price swings, not volume growth alone
red_flags: P/B of 4.19 — I pay no more than 1.5× book; at 4.19× there is zero asset backing protecting the investor
Other Income of INR 208 Cr in 2025 represents 26% of net profit — inflated earnings quality deserves scrutiny
Capex of INR 945 Cr in 2025 against OCF of INR 558 Cr — free cash flow deeply negative, business not self-funding at current investment levels
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Aegis Logistics is the most operationally credible business in this cohort by my standards: nine years of unbroken earnings growth, consistent operating cash flows, and a manageable debt load on the borrowings line. The LPG terminal and liquid storage business benefits from India's structural energy infrastructure buildout — a durable demand driver. However, quality of business and price of security are entirely different matters.

At 32.4x earnings and 4.19x book, the stock embeds optimistic assumptions about continued volume growth and margin expansion that I cannot underwrite. My Graham Number of ~INR 292 versus the INR 709 market price means I am being asked to pay a 143% premium over intrinsic value — that is not investing, it is speculation. I would revisit this business at half the current price, where a margin of safety would finally emerge.
